stem:
Neil's school keeps a farm plot and a small park as human-made ecosystems. The class debates organic manure, synthetic fertilisers, and pesticides.

Which claim best judges whether a practice supports ecosystem health?

options.text: A practice supports ecosystem health when it cuts pollution, protects biodiversity, nourishes soil, and keeps farming sustainable over time.
A practice supports ecosystem health simply because the farm is labelled a habitat rather than a human-made ecosystem.
A practice supports ecosystem health if synthetic fertilisers and pesticides raise this year's crop, with no further soil care.
A practice supports ecosystem health for every farm or park in every case, even when pollution rises and wildlife declines.

teacher.key_rationale: Human-made ecosystems support health only when design and management cut pollution, protect biodiversity, nourish soil, and keep farming sustainable. Relabelling alone, dropping soil care after a yield rise, or claiming every farm always helps all miss that hinge.
